topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture on cancer evolution, contextualises it within previous material, and sets out the learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic Mutation, Clonal Selection, and Epigenetic Reprogramming
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how successive genetic mutations drive Darwinian clonal expansion and how non-mutational epigenetic alterations can independently confer cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and the Cancer Stem Cell Hypothesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the role of tissue hierarchy, stemness properties, and specific cells of origin in initiating and propagating tumors across leukemia and colorectal cancer models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental Promotion and Stromal Dependency in Tumor Growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how microenvironmental factors, including chronic inflammation and supportive stromal interactions, provide essential permissive cues for tumor outgrowth and present therapeutic targets.

topics.label: Modern Technologies for Mapping Tumor Plasticity and Microenvironments
topics.groupedBecause: It outlines how single-cell sequencing and spatial omics technologies enable the experimental investigation of tumor evolution, cell states, and cell-cell interactions.

topics.label: Integrated Multifactorial Model of Cancer Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: It synthesises how genetic mutations, epigenetic states, cellular origin, and microenvironmental conditions converge to drive cancer progression as an evolutionary process.

topics.label: Closing Framing and Next Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture session and previews the upcoming topic of cancer therapy.
